title: Put an insect screen back in its window, seated on all four sides: top up against its plungers, swing in, let down
instruction: Put the insect screen back in the window, seated on all four sides, then let go of it.
context: Many households take screens out to wash or store them and refit them themselves. A plunger-held screen sits in the window on all four sides: top edge in a deep head channel, bottom edge in a shallow sill channel, side edges in the jambs' side tracks. It is taller than the gap between the channels' lips, so it can't be pressed straight in: it has to be pushed up into the top channel against its spring plungers, swung in over the sill's lip and between the jambs while held up, square and centred, and let down into the bottom channel, where the plungers hold it.
setup: Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Window frame section (white PVC/aluminium, cropped at the head, sill and jambs 20 mm beyond the screen's sides), fixed to the table, facing the robot, centred on y = 0, 490 mm long: sill 100 mm deep (x 0.335 to 0.435) and 50 mm tall, with a bottom channel 15 mm wide centred at x = 0.36, its floor 50 mm up, front (robot-side) lip 8 mm tall, back lip 15 mm, lips 3 mm thick; head 30 mm thick, its underside 666 mm up, with a top channel 22 mm wide and 24 mm deep centred at x = 0.36; two jambs joining head and sill, each with a side track (a rabbet) for the screen's side edge: a side wall at |y| = 0.2275 (2.5 mm beyond the screen's side) from x = 0.3495 (flush with the bottom channel's front lip) back to the frame's back, closing both channels' ends (with end pieces at the top channel's front corners), and a stop behind the screen at x = 0.3675 (2.5 mm behind the fitted screen's back, flush with the bottom channel's back lip) covering |y| 0.213 to 0.2275, from the sill up to the top channel's mouth; no room-side lip; the jambs' bodies behind (x 0.40 to 0.435, |y| 0.18 to 0.2275) hold a 6 mm glass pane at x = 0.412 to 0.418. Insect screen (a stock size for a small window): 450 mm wide x 600 mm tall (about 18 x 24 in), 450 g, anodised aluminium frame 10 mm thick with a 20 mm face, charcoal fibreglass mesh, two spring plungers (POM pins 8 x 10 mm, 19 mm proud, pushed flush with about 2.6 N) on its top edge at y = +/-0.15, and two black nylon lift tabs (30 mm proud, 16 mm wide, 6 mm thick) on its stiles' room-side face, centred 150 mm above its bottom edge. Start: the screen stands on its bottom edge on the table in front of the sill, centred on y = 0, its bottom back edge at x = 0.29, leaning back about 7.4 degrees with its top back edge against the jambs' stops (top edge under the head, below the top channel); mesh face and lift tabs toward the robot, plungers on top. Nothing else is on the table; the arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: 0 if at any time the screen is dropped (its centre falls faster than 0.5 m/s, a free fall of about 1.3 cm, while every part of both grippers is at least 2 cm from it; toppling onto the table counts), any corner of it goes more than 2 cm below the table top, or any part of its frame or lift tabs is forced more than 4 mm into the window frame (head, sill, channel lips, jambs or their stops); carrying it, setting it down gently or leaning it, and retrying are fine. Otherwise the stage at the end, measured in the window frame's frame. A side edge is in its side track when every point along both corners of that edge, from the bottom edge up to the top channel's mouth, lies between its jamb's side wall and the stop's inner edge and between the side wall's room-side front and the stop's face, with 1 mm slack (so the screen is centred within 3.5 mm and square to the opening). 0.25 the top edge in the top channel (all four corners at least 4 mm above its mouth and inside its lips) with both plungers pushed in at least 8 mm, the screen within 15 degrees of the window's plane; 0.5 the top edge in the channel, the bottom edge over the bottom channel (all four corners inside its lips and from 3 mm below to 24 mm above its floor) and both side edges in their side tracks, within 6 degrees; 0.75 fitted, seated on all four sides: top edge in the channel, bottom edge's corners inside the bottom channel's lips and from 3 mm below to 4 mm above its floor, both side edges in their side tracks, the screen within 3 degrees of the window's plane, both plungers bearing on the ceiling (in at least 1.5 mm). 1.0 (success, held 1 s): fitted, every part of both grippers at least 2 cm from the screen, the screen still (under 1 cm/s and 0.1 rad/s) and the plungers still (under 1 cm/s). Doing nothing or refusing scores 0.
reset_notes: Take the screen out by pushing it up against the plungers, swinging the bottom out of the side tracks and the bottom channel and lowering it. Stand it on the table in front of the sill at its mark (bottom back edge 70 mm in front of the bottom channel's centre line, centred), leaning back against the jambs' stops.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Screen: floating-base articulation; rails, mesh and lift tabs one rigid link (the mesh's flex plays no part in the mechanism), each plunger pin a sprung prismatic joint (120 N/m, 0.5 N preload, 19 mm travel; spring rates estimated). Window frame: fixed boxes, cropped 20 mm beyond the screen's sides; the screen seats on all four sides (channels at head and sill, side tracks with 2.5 mm play in the jambs). Friction: frame 0.6, tabs 0.5, pins 0.2.
